key_insight: CAPE extends acoustic perturbation equations to cavitating flows by embedding vapor mass transfer, mixture compressibility, and pressure-rate effects so cavitation noise can be resolved directly in the flow simulation.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical hydroacoustic tool for predicting and localizing cavitation-induced noise in marine and hydraulic systems, including cylinders and hydrofoils.
method: Formulate cavitation-consistent acoustic perturbation equations with phase-change and compressibility source terms.
Use numerical verification on 1D wave-propagation tests with a perfectly matched layer for nonreflecting boundaries.
Apply the framework to cavitating cylinder and NACA hydrofoil cases to identify radiation patterns and tonal sources.
evidence_signal: The method was verified with 1D wave-propagation problems and showed mesh/time-step convergence, suppressed boundary reflections, and attenuation consistent with Stokes' sound attenuation law.
watch_item: Accuracy may depend on reliable cavitation modeling and well-resolved phase-change regions, since localized collapse sources are highly sensitive to numerical resolution and closure assumptions.
paper_title: Cavitation Acoustic Perturbation Equations: A Computational Framework for Source-Resolved Multiphase Hydroacoustics
